transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-12 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Mariner Head of ML), Tom Bowers (Platform Lead), Sanjay Patel (CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to scope POC focused on traffic modeling and benchmark success criteria. Customer provided preliminary estimates for peak QPS and token distributions, wants a 4-week POC.

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Aisha from Redwood, Diego's here on the SE side. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Lena: Hi, Lena here. Head of ML at Mariner.
[00:15] Tom: Tom, platform.
[00:17] Sanjay: Sanjay, CTO.
[00:20] Diego: Great, thanks. Agenda is to walk through your workload shape, success criteria for the POC, and the benchmark plan. We'll also cover access and timeline.
[00:45] Lena: Cool. To set context, we run a conversational payments assistant. Typical turn is short: user asks "pay 100 to vendor X" or asks balance questions. We see a mix of single-turn and multi-turn. Peak business hours hit around 75 qps currently on inference side, but we want headroom to 100 QPS.
[01:05] Tom: Right, and our platform currently fans requests through a Node microservice which then calls the model endpoint. Right now it's hosted with an internal model but we want to compare Redwood hosted and Dedicated options.
[01:20] Aisha: Helpful. When you say 75 QPS, is that sustained or burst? Any typical concurrency per user/session?
[01:30] Lena: It's bursty. Sustained baseline around 25 qps with spikes up to 75-80 for 10-15 minute windows. Session concurrency is low (0-4), maybe 1.2 requests per active user on average for short flows. Multi-turn flows (2-6 turns) are about 15% of requests.
[01:50] Diego: Can you share token distributions — input tokens and expected output tokens? That really changes cost and latency.
[02:05] Lena: Yeah, average user input is 8-14 tokens (short), output is usually 12-34 tokens depending on whether we include confirmation. For some richer responses like dispute flows outputs can be 150-300 tokens but that's <2% of traffic.
[02:30] Sanjay: Our target is p95 latency under 300ms for typical short turns (let's say inputs <20 tokens and outputs <50 tokens). If that's possible while keeping cost under our threshold, we'd be interested in Dedicated.
[02:45] Aisha: Understood. For the POC we'll model three buckets: short (input 5-20 / output 10-50), medium (input 20-80 / output 50-150), long (<2% heavy tails). We'll run synthetic traffic to match your real token hist.
[03:05] Tom: How do you handle KV cache or prefix caching for session memory? We do a lot of session context reuse, could reduce cost if cached.
[03:20] Diego: Redwood supports automatic prefix/KV caching and batching. Quick note — sometimes transcripts show K V cash — but functionally it's KV cache. We'll instrument cache hit rates in benchmark so you can see real unit token reduction.
[03:40] Lena: Great — that could drop our token volume significantly for repeated confirmation prompts.
[03:55] Diego: For throughput modeling, we generally look at QPS, concurrency (in-flight tokens), and token/sec. For example, 100 QPS with 30 token response average is 3k output tokens/sec plus input tokens.
[04:10] Aisha: Do you have SLOs across percentiles? Most customers want p50/p95/p99.
[04:20] Sanjay: p95 is our primary gating metric. p99 is nice but lower priority. p50, p95 for short-turn flows is key.
[04:30] Aisha: Ok. Benchmarks we propose:
- Baseline single-model latency profile with your sample traffic at 25/50/100 QPS.
- Batching and cache-enabled runs to show cost delta.
- Model variant fallback tests (if Dedicated capacity constrained).
[04:55] Diego: We'll also include cold-start tests for rare long flows and measure memory utilization per model so you can compare Dedicated sizing.
[05:10] Tom: About Dedicated — what are autoscaling options? Can you burst to hosted if Dedicated saturated?
[05:22] Aisha: Yes, you can configure burst policy. Redwood Dedicated has reserve pools and optional burst to hosted regionally, or fallback to a smaller model to preserve latency. We can document SLA differences.
[05:40] Lena: Security questions — we need VPC peering or some kind of private connectivity, KMS integration for keys, SOC2 docs.
[05:50] Aisha: We'll share our security pack. For Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering, customer-managed KMS and audit logs. We'll add those docs to the SOW.
[06:05] Sanjay: For the POC timeline, we're looking at a 4-week run. Week 1: traffic sample ingestion + baseline. Week 2: configure caching/batching + tuning. Week 3: run scale tests. Week 4: analyze results and handoff. Does that align?
[06:30] Diego: Yep, that's our typical cadence. For the scale tests we need staging VPC access and an anonymized traffic sample with token distributions and percentiles.
[06:45] Tom: We can provide a 48-hour sample from prod sanitized. We'll need instructions for how to format it.
[06:52] Diego: We'll send a template. Also please include timestamps so we can replay traffic burst patterns.
[07:02] Lena: On success criteria — besides p95 < 300ms, we'd like to prove <=X cost per 1k tokens. We didn't pin X in this call but we have internal thresholds.
[07:15] Aisha: Noted. We'll run cost projections against your token mix for hosted vs Dedicated. We'll show per-token cost with and without caching.
[07:28] Sanjay: Any required firewall rules for the staging benchmark?
[07:33] Tom: We'll whitelist Redwood runner IPs once we get the list.
[07:37] Diego: We'll provide that. For benchmark tooling, we usually use a JMeter/locust style runner that hits the endpoint with a driver that injects tokens and measures latency distribution. We also include a script that simulates user think-time and session affinity to test cache effectiveness.
[08:00] Lena: How do you measure KV cache hit rates during the run?
[08:06] Diego: We emit metrics for prefix cache hits/misses via the console and can provide a CSV with per-request meta so you can correlate hits to latency and cost.
[08:18] Aisha: Any constraints around model architecture? Are you planning to bring-your-own models or use Redwood-curated ones?
[08:26] Lena: We were thinking of comparing a couple open models that are in your catalog vs our in-house tuned variant. We may start with a medium-sized Llama-family model and compare performance.
[08:38] Diego: Good. We'll recommend quantization profiles and kernel selection; for example INT8 configs can reduce memory and cost. For the POC we'll test a few quantized variants to see latency tradeoffs. Note some model names get mis-transcribed in notes but we'll call out exact flavors in the SOW.
[08:58] Tom: Regarding observability, we want token-level cost and latency breakdown per route. Is that available in the console?
[09:05] Aisha: Yes, the Redwood Console surfaces per-route latency percentiles and token-level cost. We'll enable your team in demo mode so you can see these during the POC.
[09:18] Sanjay: For the benchmark targets, can Redwood show us a projection table? Like for 75 QPS with your recommended model and caching at 50% hit rate, what's the estimated tokens/sec, cost per hour, and p95 latency?
[09:32] Diego: Yes, we'll run projection spreadsheets. We'll need your token distribution to make it accurate. We'll share an initial projection in the next couple days and refine after you provide the sample.
[09:45] Lena: Timeline for SOW and pricing?
[09:50] Aisha: I'll send SOW and pricing by Friday (2026-05-14). Once you sign, we'll schedule the benchmark for week of 2026-05-18.
[09:59] Tom: OK. A few edge questions: persistence of KV cache across restarts? And support for private deployments?
[10:08] Diego: KV cache is best-effort in-memory across the serving cluster; for long-lived session state we recommend a small session store. For Private, yes we support private control planes and on-prem packages — we can scope that but it's usually separate from a 4-week POC.
[10:25] Sanjay: If we see costs too high, what levers do we have?
[10:29] Aisha: You can adjust batching, quantization, model size, or route low-priority traffic to cheaper variants or cached responses. We'll show cost vs latency tradeoffs in the benchmark report.
[10:40] Lena: Also curious about warm-up time when switching models or using fallback.
[10:45] Diego: We'll measure cold-starts; warm-up is influenced by model size and whether KV cache is populated. We'll include warm-start measurements in the benchmarks.
[10:58] Aisha: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[11:03] Aisha: Action items: I'll send SOW/pricing and security pack; Diego will prep the benchmark harness; Mariner will share sanitized traffic and grant staging access.
[11:15] Sanjay: Sounds good.
[11:18] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[11:20] Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark run and send the templates.
[11:25] End meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: Some technical terms mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache pronounced as "K V cash", Redwood Dedicated sometimes as "Redwood Dedcated"). Occasional speaker label inconsistency observed.
